title: The Foundation of the Church
english: Goodness will certainly not be deprived of honor. No one should think that I, following the praise of brave men heard from you, will follow the laws of the wisdom of the outside. For we do not practice flattery through a composed art, but we strive to present to you, souls desiring virtue, the truth. Therefore, the silence of family lines and the pride of ancestors will not block the word. Flesh and blood shall not inherit the kingdom of God (Romans 8:3). Nor shall we honor the sky-dwellers from the worldly and earth-bound, but rather the opposite: the obscure lives of fathers, the crude arts, and the shadow called poverty shall be remembered in praises.

For the glory of Christians, according to the gospel, is our humility. I am also terribly reproached by the praises of those from without, because they, wishing to ennoble those they win over, say nothing exceptional, but they sit by the graves and disturb those lying there, making the dead into a decoration for the living; through which they call upon the departed, while confessing they have nothing good to say to those being praised by them.

And besides this, if it were true that those descending from illustrious fathers are themselves good and inherit virtue as if by some nature, it would perhaps have been timely to make some mention of the parents; but since the successions of lineage are lied about, there is even more difference in outward affectations; for the philosopher is unrefined and the lover of pleasure is a philosopher, and it is useless to remember the toil of the forefathers; it is necessary to demonstrate, if anyone has achievements of virtue. And to learn that this has such a way, one cannot learn it from meddling elsewhere, but from our own Holy Scripture, having manifold and varied usefulness.

Know certainly the priest, that elder, the nourisher and teacher of the great Samuel; but he himself, being excellent, did not benefit the sons; and having been nourished by him who begot [him] and learning the laws of the priesthood every day. And from ungodly fathers again, I speak of Timothy, the brave dog of Paul the apostle, and he certainly did not follow as if by some nature of the parents.
Having judged by reason, he hated their impiety toward the holy law of piety, and a sweet fruit appeared from a bitter root. Half-men in communion and sheep in offspring.

Thus Absalom, having been a youth toward a lenient father and so well known for audacity, as much as the father was in kindness; or rather, if it is necessary to speak the truer thing, he exceeded by a great measure in wickedness the virtue of the one who begat him. And entirely, if anyone wishes to understand with the mind this opposition of children toward fathers, he will find myriads of the diligent from the evil and the wicked from the best. And very appropriately. For if nature and not manner were performing virtue or wickedness, the two would not be, but one side would have prevailed alone.

Let Peter be called the son of Jonah; as for whose [son] this is, it makes no difference to me. For I honor the one who begat through the actions of the son; and starting from below, I send the glory to the things above, just as the lamps of the night light the ceilings from the ground. He says, prophesying Isaiah, that the Father placed the Son as a cornerstone, indicating that the whole composition of the world has its seat and its foundation in Him.

And the Only-begotten again, as he says in the gospels, names Peter the foundation of the church: 'You are Peter, and upon this rock I will build my church.' For truly this one is first like a great and enduring stone cast into the hollow of this world or the pit of lamentation, as David says, so that having supported all Christians remaining in building, he might lift them up to the height, which is the dwelling-place of our hope. Paul also calls Christ the foundation, saying: 'No one can lay a foundation other than the one laid, which is Jesus Christ.'

Our Savior, by the same designation, adorned even his first disciple, naming him a rock of faith. Therefore, through Peter, the foundation of the churches is saved, being unshakeable and unswerving, having become a true and faithful initiate of piety. Through the building of the righteous we have stood rooted, Christians from the setting sun until the rising. And having been moved by many trials since it was reported that the...

title: Theologian vs. Human Wisdom
english: The Gospel, wanting to cast down myriads of tyrants and even the devil before them and to bring us down to the ground with their foundations. Indeed the 36 rivers flowed, as the saving word says, like torrents, and fierce winds of devilish spirits struck, and the rains of those persecuting Christians burst through, and nothing stronger was seen of the fortification according to God, because the building of faith was constructed with the holy stones of the first of the apostles.

These things happened because of one word of blessing, naming the evangelist Peter. Let us see, if it seems good, how Peter builds: not with stones and bricks, nor with other earthly materials, but with words and actions made effective by the Spirit.

Therefore, when our God and Savior ascended into the heavens, while the cloud was a vehicle for the apostles to see, this man took up the teaching of the Gospel; and before all those sharing in the episcopate, opening the mouth of those raging against piety, he purified a people, and a wise orator appeared among the nations and Israel; people whose teeth were sharpened and whose minds were filled, if anyone should name Jesus.

So that what was said concerning the Lord by prophecy fits perfectly also with Peter: 'Many dogs have surrounded me, fattened bulls have enclosed me' (Psalm 71:9). But nevertheless, living by the Spirit and not grasping the command but saving what was said to him: 'Feed my lambs' (John 21:15), he cried out to a mixed people from myriads of nations; Jewish men and all those dwelling in Jerusalem.

And so that we may not speak at length, joining all the discourse together, he remembers the sayings of Joel prophesying the outpouring of the Spirit (Joel 2:28); from there he moves to David, setting forth the fifteenth psalm to confirm the resurrection (Psalm 16:10); and concluding the whole word in wisdom of words and witness of the law, he immediately led the listeners on, not ten, nor a hundred, nor three or five times so many, but three thousand men, a fullness of the church, a whole people sufficient to strike the enemies, of whom they burst through in a crowd.
Oh, how persuasive a warm and fiery medicine, having cleansed the souls so sharply! Oh, wisdom!

Theologian, having covered all human wisdom! What do you say, you who crown Demosthenes according to rhetoricians and praise Socrates among philosophers? For Demosthenes, indeed, the great and much-talkative one regarding rhetoric, held himself back so much from those things he intended to persuade by, that he was even exiled from the city by the listeners; but Socrates, for the many discourses toward the Athenians and the wise discussions, found the end in the hemlock, being killed by the chorus of disciples; such was his extent in the power of persuading.

But Peter the fisherman, the craftsman, the unlearned, whom anyone would call whatever they might wish to belittle, having hunted three thousand men with a single thrust of a word, firmly established [the church]; and these, being discontented and rioting and not forgiving him the dividing of the beginning, split the mouth.

But having come to a sufficient increase and progress of the Christian rank, since he provided a wonderful experience toward logical teachings and exhortations and practical power, having just set the lame man upright from the temple porches, that lame man who had suffered the disease from the stroke of nature in the womb of a mother, all the people rushed to the temple, being led by the fame of the great work toward the sight, and all were looking intently at the man, being struck with amazement at the wonder; the mouths of the enemies of Christ were stopped, and the cross remained a trophy of victory, not a dream.

Again the uneducated one, the worker of the prostitute's craft, begins to speak words a second time toward them, saying: 'O men, if what has happened appears to you worthy of a wonder and of divine energy, worship the healer of the lame, Jesus, whom you despised and lastly, having surpassed [him] with anger, raised up on the wood. This one is and lives; and just as it was said to you many times, having risen from the dead, he reigns over all things.'

So now, therefore, having taken up the care of those among you who have sinned, come to him and be enlightened, just as your father David says (Psalm 110:4). For if you are sons of the prophets and disciples of Moses, do not dishonor the grace of your ancestors by paying attention to lying words, but having wisely observed those things proclaimed by them, receive with your souls the Savior of your race. For this is he whom...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The greatness of Peter's miracles
english: And Moses promised that a prophet would rise up for you (Deut 18:15). Having dealt with these and similar matters, he went away, adding  others as many as the three thousands.
Such a man was indeed bold in speaking publicly, eager, undaunted, and wise for the guidance into the mysteries of the gospel, making the cowardice of his own and of his opponents a terror.

Because it was not only most diligent for the most excellent teacher of piety to labor for the great number of God's people, but much more to have the disciples live strictly according to the laws given, he saw that Ananias—that one who was a thief of his own fruits and intended to introduce a strange sacrilege and a bad habit of sin to the Christians—and he decisively cut him off from the church; he was not being crude or murderous in his intention, but in view of the purpose of benefit, he thus treated the sin as a physician.

For since the people were new converts and newly pure, having received the evangelical laws from the mixture of Greek and Jewish ways, it is expected that the disciples need not only verbal admonition, but also some practical fear; for men have somewhat habituated themselves so that, in order that they might be regulated in the beginnings of their customs, they might keep the habit until their end.

And because of this, having exposed the sin, he immediately brought death as the punishment, not using a sword, nor handing him over to executioners, but then showing the power of Christ differently in the manner of the removal. For he summoned, and the one summoned, having fallen, expired. How great this is, and how much reverence he worked in the church, we do not need to learn.

For two things were achieved in one: that our Savior be believed to be God, and that the teacher of his laws has angels accompanying him, ready, working according to the will of the apostle. He wished to benefit the lame, and the grace was not slow; he willed to punish the sacrilege, and the punishment occurred.

These things are sufficient to strike even stony souls and to persuade them firmly, that the words spoken by Peter (Acts 5:3-4) were not a deception; but God was with him and the mystery which he announced was holy and true. And it is necessary to attend to this, that the [thing] on the [other hand]...

A sign was once provided by the apostle through necessity, in folly and murder, so that those with evil intentions might be shown the power of punishment. However, the performance of benefits and healings occurred daily and continuously, and such ease and grace surrounded him in healing, so that no sick person who approached left deceived of hope, but went home whole and healthy. And every place in Jerusalem where Peter appeared to speak Christ was a place, and the crowd of following sick people had a daily wondrous spectacle from a mixed multitude, some gathered to be freed from the evils of the crowd, others to behold those being healed.

Thus also that wonderful thing concerning the apostle is written, which was not said of any of the others, that the relatives and the households of the sick brought them upon beds publicly, so that even the shadow of Peter, when he came, might overshadow some of them. This indeed is already greater than the Lord's own wonders, and the servant is praised above the Lord. And perhaps in this sign the prophecy is fulfilled, which the Savior made to the disciples: 'Amen, amen I say to you: the one believing in me the works which I do, he will do also, and he will do greater things than these' (John 14:12).

When I say this, I do not compare the servant to the Master. Away! The thought is going mad; but that God, by showing His own power through those healing by His own [power], enriched none of the disciples like Peter with his own gifts, but rather set him above all by gifts from above; and just as he became the first disciple according to the order of time, so he was shown greater than the brothers in the experience of things by the power of the Spirit.

He was called first and quickly obeyed; found by the seashores in the turbulent region of the world, always surrounded by waves and the ceaseless sound crying around the winds. He was the first among Christians to think of cosmic things, transcending all those in all things, and he was transferred toward the intelligible and the super-cosmic. And perhaps someone of the poor and obscure says, calling that thrice-blessed one: 'What...'
